name: Georgia

sales.rateNote: State sales and use tax of 4%, included in every jurisdiction's combined rate except two special Fulton County districts. Counties and cities add a stack of local option taxes (LOST, SPLOST, ESPLOST, TSPLOST, MARTA, etc.). Most vehicles pay a one-time Title Ad Valorem Tax (7.0%) instead of sales tax.

local.levies: county and municipal special purpose and local option sales taxes: LOST, SPLOST, ESPLOST (education), HOST/EHOST, TSPLOST, MARTA and Atlanta MOST, PTRLOST (property tax relief LOST); rates change quarterly

groceries.note: Food and food ingredients for off-premises consumption are exempt from the 4% state tax but subject to all local sales taxes (except the SPLOST tied to an EHOST). DOR publishes a separate food rate chart.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable at the combined state and local rate.

otherRates.item: motor vehicles (Title Ad Valorem Tax, TAVT)
otherRates.note: One-time tax on fair market value at titling, replacing sales tax and annual ad valorem tax on most vehicles; 3% for new Georgia residents, 0.5% for some family transfers.

sales.holidayNote: No Georgia sales tax holiday was found for 2026 on DOR pages.

useTax.note: Use tax is due at the same state and local rates on taxable goods bought without Georgia tax.

facts.text: The 4% state rate is part of every jurisdiction's rate except two special Fulton County districts (Central Yards and South Downtown), where only local taxes apply.
Groceries are exempt from the 4% state tax but still pay local option sales taxes.
Georgia's local taxes come as 1% building blocks such as LOST, SPLOST, ESPLOST, TSPLOST and, newly on the 2026 charts, PTRLOST for property tax relief.
Instead of sales tax, car buyers pay a one-time 7.0% Title Ad Valorem Tax on the vehicle's fair market value.
New Georgia residents pay TAVT at 3% when they title a vehicle (law effective July 1, 2019).
Local rates change by quarter; DOR publishes a new rate chart each January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1.

property.levied: Counties, school districts and cities levy millage; the county tax commissioner collects county, school and state taxes. Property is valued by the county board of assessors.

assessment.text: Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7); qualifying agricultural property under preferential assessment is taxed on 30% of fair market value. Tax = (assessed value - exemptions) x millage rate.

homestead.name: Standard Homestead Exemption
homestead.text: $2,000 deducted from the 40% assessed value of an owner-occupied primary residence, for county and school taxes (not municipal school taxes or bond debt). Many counties grant larger local exemptions or base-year valuation freezes.
homestead.applyBy: Own the home on January 1 and file with the county tax commissioner (or assessor) by the property tax return deadline, April 1, or within the 45-day assessment appeal window.

otherRelief.name: Age 65+ exemption
otherRelief.text: $4,000 exemption from county taxes if household income was $10,000 or less (retirement income excluded up to the Social Security maximum, $96,432 for 2025).

otherRelief.name: Age 62+ school tax exemption
otherRelief.text: Up to $10,000 of assessed value exempt from school taxes for low-income owners aged 62+.

otherRelief.name: Floating inflation-proof exemption (62+)
otherRelief.text: Owners aged 62+ with household income up to $30,000 can exempt increases in value above $10,000 from county taxes.

otherRelief.name: Disabled veterans
otherRelief.text: Exemption of $121,812 of value (2025 amount) from all state, county, municipal and school taxes for qualifying disabled veterans and surviving spouses.

dueDates.text: Property taxes are due by December 20 in most counties (dates vary); taxpayers have 60 days from billing to pay.

facts.text: Georgia taxes homes on 40% of market value: a $300,000 house has a $120,000 assessed value before exemptions.
The statewide homestead exemption is only $2,000 of assessed value, so county exemptions and freezes matter more.
Several counties freeze a homestead's value at a base year for as long as the owner lives there.
Property tax returns are filed between January 1 and April 1, and the owner on January 1 owes the year's tax.
Bona fide agricultural land kept in use for 10 years can be assessed at 30% of market value instead of 40%.

uncertain: HB 581 (2024) statewide floating homestead exemption (base-year value capped at inflation unless a local government opted out in 2025) was not described on the DOR pages read; not included.
Georgia DOR offers no address-based rate lookup tool on the pages read; lookupUrl points to the official quarterly rate charts.
Effective date of the 4% state rate not stated on the pages read.
The 2020 DOR exemptions list was used for the food and prescription rules (latest list linked by DOR).
